objects.description: Abstract interface for authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD). Provides pure-virtual Encrypt and Decrypt methods that take plaintext/ciphertext and associated data and return StatusOr<std::string>. Intended to be implemented by concrete AEAD primitives; thread-safe per documentation. Ownership/lifetime is governed by users of the interface; no constructors are provided here beyond a virtual destructor.

Concrete KeysetReader that parses cleartext or encrypted Tink keysets from protocol buffer binary wire format. It can be constructed via static New(...) factory methods from either an istream or a serialized bytes view. Provides Read() for Keyset and ReadEncrypted() for EncryptedKeyset. Holds an internal serialized_keyset_ buffer when constructed from a string_view. Ownership/lifetime of underlying stream for the first New overload is managed by the reader created by that factory (details not visible here).

Concrete KeysetWriter that serializes cleartext or encrypted keysets to a provided std::ostream in Protocol Buffers binary wire format. Constructed via the static New factory that takes ownership of an output stream. Write methods emit serialized proto data and return a Status indicating success or failure. The class manages the lifetime of the destination stream.

A utility class providing static helpers to read/write cleartext Tink Keysets and to convert between Keyset proto and KeysetHandle. Construction is private; there are no instances—use the static methods. Usage should be restricted because it handles key material in cleartext.

Abstract interface for deterministic authenticated encryption with associated data (DAEAD) in the crypto::tink namespace. It defines two pure-virtual methods for deterministic encryption and decryption using associated data, and a virtual destructor. Implementations must provide thread-safe, deterministic encryption semantics and authenticity/integrity for associated data; secrecy of associated data is not guaranteed. No concrete implementation details (construction, key management) are defined in this header.
This header is a thin re-export wrapper that includes tink/daead/deterministic_aead_factory.h. It does not define any custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) itself.
This header only includes another header (tink/hybrid/hybrid_config.h) and contains no type definitions, declarations, structs, enums, typedefs, or classes of its own.

Abstract interface for hybrid decryption primitives in Tink. Implementations must provide IND-CCA2-secure decryption and bind the optional context_info to the ciphertext (e.g., via AEAD associated data or as HKDF context). This header only declares the interface; no constructors are provided here. To use, obtain an implementation from the Tink keyset/registry APIs. The Decrypt method returns plaintext on success or a non-OK Status in StatusOr on failure.

Abstract interface for hybrid public-key encryption. Implementations must provide IND-CCA secure encryption and bind optional context_info to the ciphertext (e.g., via AEAD associated data or HKDF context). Provides a single pure-virtual Encrypt method returning a StatusOr<std::string> and a virtual destructor. This header only declares the interface; concrete implementations are defined elsewhere. No ownership fields are present here.

No custom types are defined in this header. It only includes another header (tink/hybrid/hybrid_key_templates.h) and contains include guards. Any types referenced are not defined here and are therefore out of scope for this extraction.

Abstract zero-copy-like input stream interface used in Tink. Implementations supply buffers via Next(), support pushing back unread bytes with BackUp(), and report the current byte position with Position(). Buffers returned by Next() are owned by the stream and remain valid only until another non-const method is called or the stream is destroyed. Next() returns StatusOr<int> where OK holds the number of bytes available; OUT_OF_RANGE indicates end-of-stream; other statuses are permanent errors.

Concrete KeysetReader that parses Google Tink Keyset and EncryptedKeyset messages encoded in proto JSON format. It can be constructed either from an input stream or from an in-memory JSON string. Provides Read and ReadEncrypted methods overriding KeysetReader to produce the respective proto objects. Ownership of underlying stream/string is managed internally.

Concrete KeysetWriter implementation that outputs cleartext or encrypted keysets in Protocol Buffers JSON wire format to a provided std::ostream. It holds an owning unique_ptr to the destination stream. Construction is via the static New factory, which returns a StatusOr with a unique_ptr to a JsonKeysetWriter. Two Write overloads serialize either a Keyset or an EncryptedKeyset to the destination. Destruction is implicit; the owned stream is closed/destroyed when the writer is destroyed. Specific error cases and formatting details are not shown in this header.

Represents a secure handle to a Tink Keyset. It abstracts access to the underlying proto holding key material, providing validated iteration over entries, reading/writing encrypted or public keysets, key generation, and primitive creation/wrapping. Construction is via static factory methods; direct constructors are mostly internal and manage secret proto ownership and monitoring annotations.

Nested type representing a single key entry within a KeysetHandle, exposing its Key object, status, numeric ID, and whether it is the primary key. Instances are constructed internally by KeysetHandle when reading or generating keysets.

A manager class for a single Tink Keyset, providing methods to add, rotate, enable, disable, destroy, delete keys, set a primary key, count keys, and obtain a KeysetHandle copy. It encapsulates a SecretProto-wrapped Keyset and uses a mutex for thread safety. Detailed semantics of Status/StatusOr and KeyTemplate are external to this header.

Abstract interface for reading Tink key material from a source. Implementations provide logic to parse and return either a cleartext Keyset or an EncryptedKeyset via StatusOr-wrapped unique_ptrs. This header only declares the interface; creation, ownership of returned keysets, and source details are implementation-specific.

Abstract interface for writing a Keyset or EncryptedKeyset to a storage destination. Implementations provide concrete storage backends (e.g., file, stream, memory). It declares two pure-virtual overloads of Write for plaintext and encrypted keysets and a virtual destructor. Construction is via derived classes; this header does not define any constructor or factory. Lifetime/ownership are managed by the user or higher-level components.

Abstract interface for clients capable of producing AEAD primitives backed by keys stored in a remote KMS. Implementations decide which key URIs they support (via DoesSupport) and can return an AEAD handle for a supported key URI (via GetAead). The class is purely virtual (interface) with a virtual destructor.

Abstract interface for Message Authentication Codes in the crypto::tink namespace. It defines two pure-virtual operations: ComputeMac to produce a MAC over input data, and VerifyMac to check a provided MAC against data. Implementations must be used only for authentication, not as a PRF or RNG. Lifetime is managed via a virtual destructor; construction is via concrete subclasses elsewhere. Return types reference util::StatusOr<std::string> and util::Status, which indicate success or detailed failure. No other types are defined in this header.

objects.description: This header is a thin umbrella/include-forwarding header that re-exports tink/mac/mac_config.h. It does not define any structs, enums, typedefs, or classes on its own.

No custom data types are defined in this header. It only includes another header (tink/mac/mac_factory.h) and contains include guards. Types referenced or defined in the included header are out of scope per instructions.

Abstract zero-copy output stream interface used by Tink. Implementations provide writable buffers via Next(), allow backing up unused tail bytes via BackUp(), support closing via Close(), and report total written bytes via Position(). No ownership or lifetime management details are specified here; callers must not retain buffer pointers beyond the next non-const call or destruction. Error handling uses util::Status/StatusOr from Tink. Details about specific implementations are unknown in this header.

Abstract interface for public key signing primitives. It defines a single pure-virtual method Sign that takes the message as an absl::string_view and returns a StatusOr<string> containing either the signature bytes or an error status. Implementations are expected to be secure against adaptive chosen-message attacks. Being an interface, it has a virtual destructor and no data members.

Abstract interface for verifying digital signatures with a public key. Implementations check that a provided signature is valid for the given data. The single method Verify returns a util::Status indicating success or failure. This is a pure virtual (interface) type; construct concrete implementations via the Tink library, not directly. Details about specific algorithms, key material, or ownership are not present in this header.

Abstract base class defining a random-access readable stream interface. Implementations must provide PRead to read up to count bytes from a given position into a provided Buffer, and size to report the logical length in bytes. No construction helpers are defined here; users obtain concrete subclasses elsewhere. Lifetime is managed by callers using pointers or smart pointers.

Global static-only registry class for managing Tink KeyManagers and PrimitiveWrappers. Provides registration APIs for key managers/wrappers and lookup/creation helpers for primitives and key data. All methods are static; instances are not intended to be created.

Abstract interface for streaming authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD). Implementations provide encrypting and decrypting stream wrappers for large data, including a random-access decrypting variant. No construction functions are defined here; users obtain concrete implementations elsewhere (e.g., via Tink key managers).

No custom data types are defined in this header. It only includes another header (tink/streamingaead/streaming_aead_key_templates.h) and provides an include guard. Any types are defined in the included header, not here.

Abstract interface for streaming message authentication codes. Provides factory methods to create output streams that either compute a MAC over streamed data or verify streamed data against a provided MAC. Implementations must supply the two pure virtual methods; this header does not define any concrete implementation details.

A simple utility class that exposes the Tink library version via a public static constexpr C-string kTinkVersion. It has no instances, data members, or methods beyond the version constant and is intended for compile-time/constant access to the version string.

functions.name: crypto::tink::Aead::Encrypt
functions.signature: virtual crypto::tink::util::StatusOr<std::string> Encrypt(absl::string_view plaintext, absl::string_view associated_data) const = 0;
functions.description: Encrypts the provided plaintext using AEAD and binds the provided associated_data for integrity/authenticity. Returns a StatusOr containing the ciphertext on success, or a non-OK status on failure. Use when you need confidentiality of plaintext and integrity/authenticity for both plaintext and associated data; associated_data itself is not encrypted.
requirements: plaintext must be accessible via absl::string_view for the duration of the call (the view must point to valid memory).
associated_data must be accessible via absl::string_view for the duration of the call (the view must point to valid memory).
Caller must check the returned StatusOr before using the ciphertext value and handle non-OK statuses appropriately.
No secrecy of associated_data is provided; do not include sensitive data there if secrecy is required.
Function may be invoked concurrently on the same Aead instance; implementations are expected to be thread safe.

functions.name: crypto::tink::Aead::Decrypt
functions.signature: virtual crypto::tink::util::StatusOr<std::string> Decrypt(absl::string_view ciphertext, absl::string_view associated_data) const = 0;
functions.description: Decrypts the provided ciphertext and verifies the integrity/authenticity of the given associated_data. Returns a StatusOr containing the recovered plaintext on success, or a non-OK status on failure (e.g., authentication failure or malformed ciphertext). Use when you have a ciphertext produced by a compatible AEAD Encrypt call.
requirements: ciphertext must be accessible via absl::string_view for the duration of the call (the view must point to valid memory).
associated_data supplied to Decrypt must exactly match the associated_data used during Encrypt for the ciphertext; otherwise decryption will fail.
Caller must check the returned StatusOr before using the plaintext value and handle non-OK statuses appropriately.
The function provides integrity/authenticity but no secrecy guarantees for associated_data.
Function may be invoked concurrently on the same Aead instance; implementations are expected to be thread safe.

functions.name: crypto::tink::Aead::~Aead
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the Aead interface, enabling safe deletion via a base-class pointer. Implementations may rely on the defaulted destructor semantics.
requirements: Object must be a valid Aead implementation instance when destroyed.
It is safe to delete through a pointer/reference to crypto::tink::Aead due to the virtual destructor.

functions.name: crypto::tink::BinaryKeysetReader::New
functions.description: Factory that creates a BinaryKeysetReader backed by an input stream containing a keyset serialized in protobuf binary wire format. Returns a StatusOr holding a KeysetReader on success or an error status if the reader cannot be constructed (e.g., invalid input). Use this when your keyset is provided via a stream (file, memory stream, etc.).
requirements: Caller transfers ownership of keyset_stream; it must be a valid, non-null std::istream.
The stream must be readable and positioned at the correct offset for the serialized keyset data.
The stream’s contents must be a cleartext google::crypto::tink::Keyset or a google::crypto::tink::EncryptedKeyset encoded in protobuf binary wire format.
Caller must check the returned StatusOr before using the contained KeysetReader.

functions.name: crypto::tink::BinaryKeysetReader::Read
functions.description: Parses and returns a cleartext google::crypto::tink::Keyset from the underlying binary protobuf data source associated with this BinaryKeysetReader. Use when you expect the input to be a cleartext Keyset. Returns an error status if the data is not a valid Keyset or cannot be read.
requirements: Must be called on a BinaryKeysetReader successfully created via New(...).
The underlying data must encode a google::crypto::tink::Keyset in protobuf binary wire format; otherwise the function returns an error status.
Caller must check the returned StatusOr before using the contained Keyset.
If constructed from a stream, the stream must be readable; read operations may consume data from the stream.

functions.name: crypto::tink::BinaryKeysetReader::ReadEncrypted
functions.description: Parses and returns a google::crypto::tink::EncryptedKeyset from the underlying binary protobuf data source associated with this BinaryKeysetReader. Use when you expect the input to be an EncryptedKeyset. Returns an error status if the data is not a valid EncryptedKeyset or cannot be read.
requirements: Must be called on a BinaryKeysetReader successfully created via New(...).
The underlying data must encode a google::crypto::tink::EncryptedKeyset in protobuf binary wire format; otherwise the function returns an error status.
Caller must check the returned StatusOr before using the contained EncryptedKeyset.
If constructed from a stream, the stream must be readable; read operations may consume data from the stream.

functions.name: crypto::tink::BinaryKeysetWriter::New
functions.description: Factory method that creates a BinaryKeysetWriter which writes keysets to the provided std::ostream in protobuf binary wire format. Ownership of the output stream is transferred to the writer. Returns a StatusOr that contains the constructed writer on success or an error status on failure. Typical usage: pass a heap-allocated std::ostream (e.g., a std::unique_ptr<std::ofstream>) and then use Write() to serialize a Keyset or EncryptedKeyset.
requirements: destination_stream must be a non-null unique_ptr to a valid, writable std::ostream.
Ownership of destination_stream is transferred; the caller must not use the stream after calling New (the pointer is moved).
The underlying stream must be in a good state (e.g., not already failed/closed) and capable of accepting binary output.
Callers must check the returned StatusOr for ok() before using the contained writer; on error, the contained pointer must not be accessed.

functions.name: crypto::tink::BinaryKeysetWriter::Write
functions.description: Serializes the given cleartext Keyset protobuf to the writer's destination stream using protobuf binary wire format. Returns a Status indicating success or failure. Intended to be called on a writer created via New().
requirements: A BinaryKeysetWriter instance must have been successfully created via New() and still own a valid, writable destination stream.
keyset must be a properly initialized google::crypto::tink::Keyset protobuf object (non-null reference as per signature).
The caller must check the returned Status and handle errors; no output is guaranteed on failure.
The destination stream must be writable and not in a failed state at the time of the call.

functions.name: crypto::tink::CleartextKeysetHandle::Read
functions.signature: static crypto::tink::util::StatusOr<std::unique_ptr<crypto::tink::KeysetHandle>> Read(std::unique_ptr<crypto::tink::KeysetReader> reader, const absl::flat_hash_map<std::string, std::string>& monitoring_annotations = {})
functions.description: Creates a KeysetHandle by reading a cleartext keyset from the supplied KeysetReader. Optionally attaches monitoring annotations (string key/value pairs) to the resulting handle for monitoring use. Intended for restricted use because it loads cleartext key material into memory. Returns a StatusOr that must be checked before use.
requirements: reader must own a valid KeysetReader capable of producing a cleartext google::crypto::tink::Keyset
monitoring_annotations may be empty; keys and values are strings; no other constraints are specified
caller must check the returned StatusOr and only use the KeysetHandle if status is OK
use of this API should be restricted as it handles cleartext key material (as stated in comments)

functions.name: crypto::tink::CleartextKeysetHandle::Write
functions.signature: static crypto::tink::util::Status Write(crypto::tink::KeysetWriter* writer, const crypto::tink::KeysetHandle& keyset_handle)
functions.description: Writes the cleartext keyset contained in the given KeysetHandle to the provided KeysetWriter. Intended for restricted use because it emits cleartext key material. Returns a Status indicating success or failure.
requirements: writer must be non-null
writer must be ready/initialized to accept a cleartext keyset (e.g., opened/positioned as required by the specific KeysetWriter implementation)
caller must check the returned Status for errors
the provided keyset_handle must contain a keyset; no other constraints are documented

functions.name: crypto::tink::CleartextKeysetHandle::GetKeysetHandle
functions.description: Constructs and returns a KeysetHandle that wraps the provided cleartext Keyset proto. Intended for situations where the key material is already available in cleartext and needs to be represented as a KeysetHandle.
requirements: keyset must be a valid google::crypto::tink::Keyset proto
callers should treat the resulting handle as containing cleartext key material and restrict its use (per class-level comment)

functions.name: crypto::tink::CleartextKeysetHandle::GetKeyset
functions.signature: static const google::crypto::tink::Keyset& GetKeyset(const crypto::tink::KeysetHandle& keyset_handle)
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the underlying cleartext Keyset proto contained in the given KeysetHandle. Useful for direct proto-level access when working with cleartext key material.
requirements: keyset_handle must refer to a KeysetHandle that exposes an underlying cleartext google::crypto::tink::Keyset (consistent with CleartextKeysetHandle usage); if not, behavior is implementation-defined/unknown (inferred due to lack of explicit documentation)
the returned reference remains valid as long as keyset_handle remains alive and unchanged (typical for returning a reference; exact lifetime semantics are not explicitly documented)

functions.name: crypto::tink::DeterministicAead::EncryptDeterministically
functions.signature: virtual crypto::tink::util::StatusOr<std::string> EncryptDeterministically(absl::string_view plaintext, absl::string_view associated_data) const = 0;
functions.description: Deterministically encrypts the given plaintext using the provided associated_data as associated (non-secret) data, returning a ciphertext that authenticates both the plaintext and the associated data. Because encryption is deterministic, the same (plaintext, associated_data, key) tuple yields the same ciphertext. Callers should use this to obtain authenticated encryption where AAD integrity is enforced; secrecy of associated_data is not provided.
requirements: plaintext may be empty or arbitrary bytes; it must be addressable for the duration of the call (absl::string_view does not own the data).
associated_data may be empty or arbitrary bytes; it must be addressable for the duration of the call (absl::string_view does not own the data).
Callers must not modify or free the memory referenced by plaintext or associated_data while the call is in progress.
Callers must check the returned StatusOr; on error, do not use the value.
Determinism implies that using identical plaintext and associated_data under the same key will produce identical ciphertexts (do not rely on semantic security against equality leakage).

functions.name: crypto::tink::DeterministicAead::DecryptDeterministically
functions.signature: virtual crypto::tink::util::StatusOr<std::string> DecryptDeterministically(absl::string_view ciphertext, absl::string_view associated_data) const = 0;
functions.description: Deterministically decrypts the given ciphertext verifying the integrity and authenticity of the provided associated_data, returning the recovered plaintext on success. The associated_data must be identical to what was used at encryption time; associated_data is authenticated but not kept secret.
requirements: ciphertext must be a valid ciphertext produced by the same key/primitive and algorithm; it must be addressable for the duration of the call (absl::string_view does not own the data).
associated_data must exactly match the data used during encryption; it must be addressable for the duration of the call.
Callers must not modify or free the memory referenced by ciphertext or associated_data while the call is in progress.
Callers must check the returned StatusOr; on error (e.g., authentication failure or malformed input), do not use the value.
Do not assume any secrecy for associated_data; only authenticity and integrity are provided.

functions.name: crypto::tink::DeterministicAead::~DeterministicAead
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the DeterministicAead interface, enabling safe deletion via a base-class pointer.
requirements: Objects of types derived from DeterministicAead may be deleted through a DeterministicAead* safely.
Callers must ensure no use-after-destruction; do not call interface methods after the object has been destroyed.

functions.name: crypto::tink::HybridDecrypt::Decrypt
functions.signature: virtual crypto::tink::util::StatusOr<std::string> Decrypt(absl::string_view ciphertext, absl::string_view context_info) const = 0;
functions.description: Decrypts the given ciphertext and verifies that the provided context_info matches what was used at encryption time. Returns the plaintext on success wrapped in StatusOr, or an error status on failure. This is a pure-virtual method of crypto::tink::HybridDecrypt; concrete implementations provide the actual decryption. Use when you need to recover plaintext produced by a corresponding HybridEncrypt primitive while binding public, non-secret context information to the ciphertext. Note: hybrid encryption provides privacy but not sender authentication.
requirements: Caller must provide ciphertext that was produced by a compatible HybridEncrypt using the corresponding key/parameters.
Caller must provide the identical context_info value that was used during encryption; it may be empty. If the values do not match, decryption will fail.
Caller must check the returned StatusOr before accessing the plaintext value and handle error statuses appropriately.
context_info is public data; do not assume secrecy or authenticity from this parameter.
Method is const; no object mutation is expected or relied upon by the caller.

functions.name: crypto::tink::HybridDecrypt::~HybridDecrypt
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the HybridDecrypt interface. Ensures proper cleanup via base-class pointers. Defaulted implementation; concrete implementations may define their own destructors as needed.
requirements: Do not use the object after the destructor has run (standard C++ object lifetime rules).
If held via a base-class pointer, ensure the destructor is virtual (already provided) so derived resources are released correctly.

functions.name: crypto::tink::HybridEncrypt::Encrypt
functions.signature: virtual crypto::tink::util::StatusOr<std::string> Encrypt(absl::string_view plaintext, absl::string_view context_info) const = 0;
functions.description: Encrypts the given plaintext and binds the supplied context_info to the resulting ciphertext. Implementations are intended to be secure against adaptive chosen-ciphertext attacks. The context_info is typically public, is integrity-bound to the ciphertext, and must be provided unchanged to the corresponding HybridDecrypt during decryption to succeed. Returns a StatusOr containing the ciphertext on success or an error status on failure.
requirements: plaintext must be provided as a valid absl::string_view whose referenced memory remains valid for the duration of the call.
context_info may be empty; it should be the same value supplied during decryption to enable successful verification and decryption.
Callers must check the returned crypto::tink::util::StatusOr before using the contained ciphertext; do not assume success.
May be called via a const HybridEncrypt instance; thread-safety is not specified in this interface.

functions.name: crypto::tink::HybridEncrypt::~HybridEncrypt
functions.description: Virtual defaulted destructor for the HybridEncrypt interface, enabling proper cleanup of derived implementations when deleted via a base-class pointer. Not intended to be invoked directly by callers.
requirements: Objects should be destroyed through normal C++ object lifetime management (e.g., delete or smart pointers) rather than calling the destructor explicitly.
Safe destruction requires that no outstanding operations are using the object at the time of destruction (general C++ requirement).

functions.name: crypto::tink::InputStream::InputStream
functions.description: Default constructor for the abstract InputStream interface. Creates an instance of an InputStream subclass (via derived classes) that supports zero-copy style reads. Use via a concrete implementation.
requirements: Must be invoked on a concrete subclass (InputStream itself is abstract).
No explicit input/state requirements are documented.

functions.name: crypto::tink::InputStream::~InputStream
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the InputStream interface. Ensures proper cleanup via base pointers.
requirements: Callers must not access any buffer previously obtained from Next() after the stream is destroyed, as ownership remains with the stream and validity ends at destruction.

functions.name: crypto::tink::InputStream::Next
functions.description: Obtains the next contiguous chunk of bytes from the stream without copying (zero-copy). On success returns the number of bytes in the chunk and sets *data to an internal buffer; on OUT_OF_RANGE there is no more data (EOF); any other non-OK status indicates a permanent error. The returned buffer remains owned by the stream and is only valid until the next non-const method call or stream destruction. Zero-length buffers may be returned; callers should keep calling until a non-zero buffer or a non-OK status is returned.
requirements: Argument data must not be NULL (non-null pointer to receive the buffer pointer).
Caller must treat the returned StatusOr<int>: OK indicates bytes read; OUT_OF_RANGE indicates end-of-stream; any other non-OK is a permanent error and reading should stop.
Caller must not write to the returned buffer and must not retain or use the pointer after any subsequent non-const method call on the stream (e.g., Next(), BackUp()) or after the stream is destroyed.
Caller must tolerate zero-sized buffers and may need to call Next() repeatedly until a non-zero-sized buffer is obtained or a non-OK status is returned.

functions.name: crypto::tink::InputStream::BackUp
functions.description: Pushes back up to count bytes from the last buffer returned by Next() so they will be returned again on subsequent Next() calls. Useful to unread data that went beyond what was needed.
requirements: BackUp should only be called after a Next() call that returned status OK; if there was no successful Next() or the last Next() failed, BackUp is ignored.
count should be non-negative; non-positive values are ignored (no action).
For intended behavior, count must be less than or equal to the size of the last buffer returned by Next(); larger values are treated as the last buffer's size.
The effect of BackUp() accumulates over multiple calls and can be verified via Position().
Do not assume BackUp() affects any buffer validity beyond what is stated for Next(); previously returned buffers remain invalid after calling a non-const method.

functions.name: crypto::tink::InputStream::Position
functions.description: Returns the current byte position in the stream. If the last Next() reached end-of-stream (OUT_OF_RANGE), the position equals the total number of bytes. If the last Next() ended with a failure, returns -1.
requirements: For a meaningful position, the last call to Next() must have ended with status OK or OUT_OF_RANGE; otherwise -1 is returned.
Callers should check for -1 to detect that the last Next() failed before using the position value.

functions.name: crypto::tink::JsonKeysetReader::New
functions.description: Creates a JsonKeysetReader that will read a keyset from the provided input stream containing a proto JSON representation of a google.crypto.tink.Keyset or google.crypto.tink.EncryptedKeyset. Returns either a KeysetReader on success or an error status. Typical usage: construct via New(...), then call Read() for cleartext keysets or ReadEncrypted() for encrypted keysets.
requirements: keyset_stream must be non-null and refer to a stream containing a keyset in Protocol Buffers JSON format (google.crypto.tink.Keyset or google.crypto.tink.EncryptedKeyset).
Ownership of keyset_stream is transferred to the reader; the caller must not use the stream after passing it to this function.
Callers must check the returned StatusOr before using the contained KeysetReader and handle errors appropriately.
Thread-safety and reusability of the returned reader are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: crypto::tink::JsonKeysetReader::Read
functions.description: Parses and returns a cleartext google.crypto.tink.Keyset from the underlying JSON source. If the source does not contain a valid cleartext Keyset in proto JSON format or parsing fails, returns an error status. Typically called on a reader created by JsonKeysetReader::New.
requirements: Must be called on a JsonKeysetReader successfully created via JsonKeysetReader::New(...).
The underlying data must represent a google.crypto.tink.Keyset in Protocol Buffers JSON format; otherwise the function returns an error.
Callers must check the returned StatusOr before using the Keyset and handle errors appropriately.
Whether this function can be called multiple times on the same reader is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: crypto::tink::JsonKeysetReader::ReadEncrypted
functions.description: Parses and returns a google.crypto.tink.EncryptedKeyset from the underlying JSON source. If the source does not contain a valid EncryptedKeyset in proto JSON format or parsing fails, returns an error status. Typically used when the keyset is stored encrypted and needs to be read before decryption by a suitable key management component.
requirements: Must be called on a JsonKeysetReader successfully created via JsonKeysetReader::New(...).
The underlying data must represent a google.crypto.tink.EncryptedKeyset in Protocol Buffers JSON format; otherwise the function returns an error.
Callers must check the returned StatusOr before using the EncryptedKeyset and handle errors appropriately.
Whether this function can be called multiple times on the same reader is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: crypto::tink::JsonKeysetWriter::New
functions.description: Factory method that creates a JsonKeysetWriter that writes keysets in protobuf JSON wire format to the provided output stream. Ownership of the destination stream is transferred to the writer. Use this to obtain a writer instance before calling Write(). Returns a non-OK StatusOr on construction/parameter errors.
requirements: destination_stream must be a valid, non-null std::ostream instance intended for writing.
Ownership of destination_stream is transferred; the caller must not use the stream after passing it to New.
The stream should be in a good state (e.g., open, not failed) and writable at the time of construction.
Callers must check the returned StatusOr before using the contained writer (i.e., verify status is OK and then move the unique_ptr).

functions.name: crypto::tink::JsonKeysetWriter::Write

functions.name: crypto::tink::RandomAccessStream::PRead
functions.signature: virtual crypto::tink::util::Status crypto::tink::RandomAccessStream::PRead(int64_t position, int count, crypto::tink::util::Buffer* dest_buffer) = 0
functions.description: Reads up to 'count' bytes starting at absolute byte 'position' in the stream into 'dest_buffer'. Intended for random-access reads similar to pread on files. On success (OK), either exactly 'count' bytes are read or fewer bytes are read when the shortage may be transient; in that case the buffer is resized to the number of bytes actually read. Returns OUT_OF_RANGE when the end of stream is reached or when 'position' exceeds the current stream size. Callers should check the returned Status and use the bytes and updated size in 'dest_buffer' accordingly.

count must be positive.
dest_buffer must be non-null.
dest_buffer’s allocated size must be at least 'count' before the call.

Callers must check the returned Status: OK indicates data was read (possibly fewer than 'count' bytes with buffer resized); OUT_OF_RANGE indicates end-of-stream or position beyond size; INVALID_ARGUMENT indicates bad inputs; other statuses indicate other errors.
If OK is returned with fewer than 'count' bytes read, the shortage is not permanent and retrying may succeed (callers should be prepared to handle short reads).

functions.name: crypto::tink::RandomAccessStream::size

functions.name: crypto::tink::StreamingAead::NewEncryptingStream
functions.description: Creates and returns a wrapper OutputStream that AEAD-encrypts all bytes written to it, using the provided associated_data as Associated Authenticated Data (AAD). The AAD is not included in the ciphertext and must be provided again for decryption. The wrapper’s ByteCount() reports the number of plaintext bytes written; closing the wrapper also closes the wrapped ciphertext_destination stream. Typical usage: open a destination stream, call NewEncryptingStream, write plaintext to the returned stream, then close it to finalize.

Callers must close the returned encrypting stream to finalize encryption and to close the underlying ciphertext_destination.
Callers must check the returned crypto::tink::util::StatusOr before using the contained std::unique_ptr<crypto::tink::OutputStream> (i.e., handle error status).

functions.name: crypto::tink::StreamingAead::NewDecryptingStream
functions.description: Creates and returns a wrapper InputStream that AEAD-decrypts data read from ciphertext_source, using associated_data as AAD. The bytes read from the wrapper are plaintext, and the wrapper’s ByteCount() reports plaintext bytes read. Typical usage: open a ciphertext source stream, call NewDecryptingStream with the same AAD used for encryption, then read plaintext from the returned stream.
requirements: ciphertext_source must be a valid, readable crypto::tink::InputStream (owned via the passed std::unique_ptr).
Callers must supply the same associated_data that was used during encryption or decryption will fail authentication.
Callers must check the returned crypto::tink::util::StatusOr before using the contained std::unique_ptr<crypto::tink::InputStream> (i.e., handle error status).

functions.name: crypto::tink::StreamingAead::NewDecryptingRandomAccessStream

The returned wrapper allows random-access reads of plaintext. Note: the wrapper’s size() reports a value that is not integrity-checked; truncation or tampering may only be detected when reading the last block. Reading through the wrapper is thread-safe.
requirements: ciphertext_source must be a valid crypto::tink::RandomAccessStream capable of providing random-access reads (owned via the passed std::unique_ptr).
Callers must supply the same associated_data that was used during encryption to authenticate successfully.
Callers must check the returned crypto::tink::util::StatusOr before using the contained std::unique_ptr<crypto::tink::RandomAccessStream> (i.e., handle error status).
Callers should not rely on size() for integrity; correctness is verified when reading the final block (integrity is only guaranteed upon read).

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: generic string used as a KMS key URI candidate for KmsClient::DoesSupport
# Goal: Produce valid, interesting URI-like strings that cover common KMS schemes and edge cases,
# while remaining deterministic given a seed.

SCHEMES = [
    # Common cloud KMS URIs (various real-world-like patterns)
    "gcp-kms://projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{ring}/cryptoKeys/{key}",
    "gcp-kms://projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{ring}/cryptoKeys/{key}/cryptoKeyVersions/{version}",
    "aws-kms://arn:aws:kms:{region}:{account}:key/{uuid}",
    "aws-kms://alias/{alias}",
    "azure-kms://{vault}.vault.azure.net/keys/{key}/{version}",
    # Generic/custom schemes sometimes used by tests
    "kek://{name}",
    "kms://{name}",
    "local-kms://{name}",
    # With query params and fragments
    "gcp-kms://projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{ring}/cryptoKeys/{key}?aad={aad}&alt=json#frag",
    "aws-kms://arn:aws:kms:{region}:{account}:alias/{alias}?ctx={aad}",
]

PROJECT_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-"
RING_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-"
KEY_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_"
ALIAS_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_/."
VAULT_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-"
NAME_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_/."
AAD_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "+/=_-."

REGIONS = [
    "us-east-1", "us-west-2", "eu-west-1", "ap-southeast-1", "us-central1",
]
LOCATIONS = ["us", "us-central1", "europe-west1", "asia-east1"]


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, s: str, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(s) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_uuid(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate canonical UUIDv4-like string
    hexchars = string.hexdigits.lower()
    parts = [8, 4, 4, 4, 12]
    out = []
    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
        if i == 2:
            # version nibble = 4xxx
            seg = [rng.choice(hexchars) for _ in range(p)]
            seg[0] = '4'
            out.append("".join(seg))
        elif i == 3:
            # variant nibble: 8..b
            first = rng.choice("89ab")
            seg = [rng.choice(hexchars) for _ in range(p)]
            seg[0] = first
            out.append("".join(seg))
        else:
            out.append("".join(rng.choice(hexchars) for _ in range(p)))
    return "-".join(out)


def _maybe_with_prefix_suffix(rng: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    # Add optional whitespace, URL encoding or surrounding text to explore parsing
    options: List[str] = [base]
    options.append(base + "\n")
    options.append("\t" + base)
    options.append(base + " ")
    options.append(base.replace("://", ":/%2F/%2F", 1))  # escaped slashes after scheme
    options.append(base.replace("/", "%2F"))
    return rng.choice(options)


def _build_uri(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    tmpl = rng.choice(SCHEMES)
    substitutions = {
        "project": _rand_choice(rng, PROJECT_CHARS, 3, 20),
        "location": rng.choice(LOCATIONS),
        "ring": _rand_choice(rng, RING_CHARS, 3, 16),
        "key": _rand_choice(rng, KEY_CHARS, 3, 24),
        "version": str(rng.randint(1, 99)),
        "region": rng.choice(REGIONS),
        "account": str(rng.randint(10**11, 10**12 - 1)),
        "uuid": _rand_uuid(rng),
        "alias": _rand_choice(rng, ALIAS_CHARS, 3, 24),
        "vault": _rand_choice(rng, VAULT_CHARS, 3, 24),
        "name": _rand_choice(rng, NAME_CHARS, 1, 40),
        "aad": _rand_choice(rng, AAD_CHARS, 0, 24),
    }
    uri = tmpl.format(**substitutions)

    # Occasionally produce boundary/edge variants: empty AAD, missing fragments, or uppercase scheme
    edge_roll = rng.random()
    if edge_roll < 0.1:
        # Uppercase scheme
        if "://" in uri:
            scheme, rest = uri.split("://", 1)
            uri = scheme.upper() + "://" + rest
    elif edge_roll < 0.2:
        # Remove query string
        q = uri.find("?")
        if q != -1:
            uri = uri[:q]
    elif edge_roll < 0.3:
        # Only scheme (minimal)
        scheme = uri.split(":", 1)[0]
        uri = scheme + "://"
    elif edge_roll < 0.4:
        # Add extra path segments
        uri = uri.rstrip("/") + "/" + _rand_choice(rng, NAME_CHARS, 1, 10)

    # Optional prefix/suffix/escaping variants
    uri = _maybe_with_prefix_suffix(rng, uri)

    # Ensure length limit for fuzzer input (under 4096 bytes total). Truncate softly.
    if len(uri) > 4000:
        uri = uri[:4000]
    return uri


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Mix in variability per call with a bounded number of URIs concatenated by newlines.
    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR may be called multiple times; providing a corpus line with multiple
    # URIs allows the engine to split/trim and feed different slices.
    count = rng.randint(1, 5)
    uris = []
    # Include some canonical fixed samples to quickly hit positive matches in typical clients
    fixed_pool = [
        "gcp-kms://projects/p/locations/us/keyRings/r/cryptoKeys/k",
        "aws-kms://arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000",
        "azure-kms://myvault.vault.azure.net/keys/mykey/1",
        "kms://test-key",
        "local-kms://dev",
    ]
    for i in range(count):
        if rng.random() < 0.35:
            uris.append(rng.choice(fixed_pool))
        else:
            uris.append(_build_uri(rng))

    payload = "\n".join(uris)
    return payload.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary binary data
# Target stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR for:
# - FuzzInputStream: arbitrary bytes fed to an InputStream.
# - FuzzPublicKeySign: a salt string (<=64 bytes recommended) used to construct a signer.
# We must return a single bytes buffer that the harness will slice into FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# Since we cannot control splitting directly, we design a self-describing container with
# multiple concatenated chunks so that the first FUZZ_PARAM_STR sees a plausibly large
# payload (stream content), and the second FUZZ_PARAM_STR sees a smaller salt-like chunk.
# If the harness reuses the same buffer independently per FUZZ_PARAM_STR, both chunks
# individually are still valid arbitrary data.
#
# Format we emit (all little-endian where applicable):
# [magic 4B] 'TSTK'
# [version 1B] 0x01
# [flags 1B] bitfield (currently 0..3 random)
# [stream_len 2B] N (0..3500)
# [stream payload N bytes]
# [salt_len 1B] M (0..64)
# [salt M bytes]
# [pad_len 1B] P (0..32)
# [pad P bytes random]
# This keeps total size <= 4096.

ALPHANUM = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
PRINTABLE_EXTRA = b"-_#:.@/+=,()[]{}"  # useful varied characters


def _rand_printable_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    pool = ALPHANUM + PRINTABLE_EXTRA
    return bytes(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_binary_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return rng.randbytes(n) if hasattr(rng, "randbytes") else bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_stream_payload(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a payload that mixes printable segments, zero runs, and random bytes
    # to exercise chunking and BackUp behavior in FuzzInputStream.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = n
    patterns = ["printable", "zeros", "random", "pattern"]
    while remaining > 0:
        kind = rng.choice(patterns)
        # segment size 1..min(256, remaining)
        seg = rng.randint(1, min(256, remaining))
        if kind == "printable":
            parts.append(_rand_printable_bytes(rng, seg))
        elif kind == "zeros":
            parts.append(b"\x00" * seg)
        elif kind == "random":
            parts.append(_rand_binary_bytes(rng, seg))
        else:  # repeating pattern like ABC...
            base = _rand_printable_bytes(rng, rng.randint(3, 12))
            reps = (seg + len(base) - 1) // len(base)
            chunk = (base * reps)[:seg]
            parts.append(chunk)
        remaining -= seg
    return b"".join(parts)


def _make_salt(rng: random.Random, m: int) -> bytes:
    # Salt should be sane printable bytes to be visible and consistent when appended.
    return _rand_printable_bytes(rng, m)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose sizes with bias toward interesting values.
    # Stream length: pick from a distribution to cover small, boundary, and larger values.
    choices = [0, 1, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 3072]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        stream_len = rng.choice(choices)
    else:
        stream_len = rng.randint(0, 3500)

    # Salt length up to 64.
    salt_len_choices = [0, 1, 2, 8, 16, 32, 48, 64]
    salt_len = rng.choice(salt_len_choices) if rng.random() < 0.7 else rng.randint(0, 64)

    # Padding length small tail to vary total buffer size and ensure <=4096.
    pad_len = rng.randint(0, 32)

    stream_payload = _make_stream_payload(rng, stream_len)
    salt = _make_salt(rng, salt_len)
    pad = _rand_binary_bytes(rng, pad_len)

    # Flags: bit0 maybe indicates stream mostly printable; bit1 zeros present; bit2 random present.
    def analyze_flags(data: bytes) -> int:
        if not data:
            return 0
        is_printable_ratio = sum(32 <= b <= 126 for b in data) / len(data)
        has_zero = 1 if 0 in data else 0
        # crude randomness indicator: number of distinct bytes
        distinct = len(set(data))
        randish = 1 if distinct > min(64, max(8, len(data)//4)) else 0
        flags = 0
        if is_printable_ratio > 0.7:
            flags |= 0x1
        if has_zero:
            flags |= 0x2
        if randish:
            flags |= 0x4
        return flags & 0xFF

    flags = analyze_flags(stream_payload)

    header = b"TSTK" + struct.pack("<BBH", 1, flags, stream_len)
    body = stream_payload + struct.pack("<B", salt_len) + salt + struct.pack("<B", pad_len) + pad
    out = header + body

    # Ensure max size limit.
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]
    return out
